entities.name: Octo
entities.description: The platform context for the BCC configuration methodology described in the guide, used to build conversational form agents.

entities.name: BCC Configuration
entities.description: A configuration workflow within Octo for setting up brand/content/campaign forms via a conversational agent.

entities.name: Conversational Form Agent
entities.description: An AI agent that collects structured information through conversational interfaces, one question at a time.

entities.name: State Injection Mechanism
entities.description: The mechanism of injecting current step, total steps, and previously collected answers into the system prompt on every turn to prevent state amnesia.

entities.name: Validation Layer
entities.description: An application-side typed validation layer that determines whether an answer is valid before advancing the step counter.

entities.name: Anti-Drift Instructions
entities.description: Prompt-engineering instructions and few-shot examples that override the model's default helpfulness instinct to keep it on-task.

entities.name: Tangent Detection
entities.description: A lightweight application-side pattern-matching layer that intercepts off-topic input before it reaches the model.

entities.name: State Object
entities.description: A flat, minimal, serialisable object holding currentStep, totalSteps, answers, redirectCount, conditionalSkips, and done flags, injected into every prompt.

entities.name: Conditional Branching Logic
entities.description: Application-layer logic (getNextStep function) that handles which steps appear based on prior answers, keeping branching out of the prompt.

entities.name: Step Schema
entities.description: A reusable schema defining each form step with id, question, hint, inputType, options, required, condition, validate, and quickReplies fields.

entities.name: System Prompt Template
entities.description: A reusable system prompt template with placeholders for current state, rules, tangent handling, and completion behavior.

entities.name: Multi-Agent Architecture
entities.description: An advanced architecture splitting responsibility across a Controller agent, Responder agent, and optional FAQ handler to make drift structurally impossible.

entities.name: Controller Agent
entities.description: Owns the state machine, decides which step is active, validates answers, and handles branching; never exposed to the user directly.

entities.name: Responder Agent
entities.description: Handles only the current step with a narrow context window and generates natural-sounding responses.

entities.name: FAQ Handler Agent
entities.description: Optional third agent that handles tangential questions and returns a flag to bring the user back to the form.

entities.name: Topic Drift
entities.description: Failure mode where the agent answers unrelated questions mid-form and loses track of the current step.

entities.name: State Amnesia
entities.description: Failure mode where the model forgets which question it was on without explicit state management.

entities.name: Premature Completion
entities.description: Failure mode where the agent interprets a partial answer as sufficient and skips required fields.

entities.name: Implementation Checklist
entities.description: A checklist covering pre-coding planning, system prompt requirements, application-layer requirements, and UX requirements for building a form agent.

entities.name: Progress Indicator UX
entities.description: UX pattern showing [Question N of Total] on every agent turn so users see their position in the form.

entities.name: Quick Replies
entities.description: Suggested response chips shown to the user where the answer space is bounded.

entities.name: Live Form Preview
entities.description: UX pattern where form output is visually separate from the conversation as a live preview.

entities.name: Redirect Count Metric
entities.description: Counter tracked for analytics and for triggering escalation after N redirects when the user repeatedly goes off-topic.

relationships.description: BCC Configuration is a setup workflow that lives within the Octo platform.
The conversational form agent is the mechanism that drives the BCC configuration experience.
The form agent depends on state injection on every turn to maintain ground truth.
The form agent relies on the typed validation layer to gate state transitions.
The form agent uses anti-drift prompt instructions to override default helpfulness.
The form agent uses application-side tangent detection to intercept off-topic input.
State injection serialises and injects the state object into the prompt every turn.
The system prompt template embeds fields from the state object as runtime placeholders.
The validation layer uses the validate() function defined per step in the step schema.
getNextStep reads from answers and conditionalSkips in the state object to decide the next step.
Each step's condition function feeds into the branching logic that determines visibility.
The multi-agent architecture includes the controller agent owning the state machine.
The multi-agent architecture includes a responder agent scoped to the current step.
The multi-agent architecture optionally includes an FAQ handler for tangential questions.
The controller agent invokes the validation layer to gate step transitions.
The controller agent applies conditional branching logic to decide the next active step.
Tangent detection is the mechanism designed to mitigate topic drift.
State injection on every turn is the mitigation for state amnesia.
Typed validation prevents premature completion by rejecting partial answers.
The implementation checklist includes verifying the system prompt requirements before shipping.
The implementation checklist requires writing the step schema for each question before coding.
The checklist requires defining a tangent pattern list for the domain.
The agent surfaces a [Question N of Total] indicator on every turn.
The agent presents quick reply suggestions when the answer space is bounded.
The BCC configuration UX shows a live form preview separated from the conversation.
The state object tracks redirectCount as a field for analytics and escalation.
